snapshots.name: Ingmar Ingmarsson
snapshots.subtitle: Young heir of the Ingmar Farm
snapshots.body: The young farmer introduced plowing his field in the opening pages, proud of managing the Ingmar Farm as well as any who has borne the family name before him — the latest in a long line of Ingmar Ingmarssons whose choices will shape the whole community's fate.

snapshots.name: Big Ingmar
snapshots.subtitle: Ingmar's late father
snapshots.body: The previous head of the Ingmar Farm, remembered in the family's own stories as a shrewd and quietly commanding figure — invoked by name even after his death, as when a servant jokes that it was surely Big Ingmar who arranged an inconvenient errand from beyond the grave.

snapshots.name: Karin Ingmarsson
snapshots.subtitle: Ingmar's sister
snapshots.body: Ingmar's sister, recognized on sight by an old neighbor as 'Karin, daughter of Ingmar' — a young woman whose long, uncertain courtship by Tims Halvor is one of the threads the community watches closely.

snapshots.name: Tims Halvor
snapshots.subtitle: The shopkeeper courting Karin
snapshots.body: A young peasant, properly named Halvor Halvorsson, who came from Tims Farm and opened a shop in the village — tall and good-looking, and long engaged in a courtship of Karin that the whole parish has an opinion about.

snapshots.name: Gertrude
snapshots.subtitle: The schoolmaster's daughter
snapshots.body: The schoolmaster's daughter, first glimpsed as a fair little girl playing alone by the fire while her parents talk in worried whispers about the coming of a mission house — a child who grows into one of the book's central young women.

snapshots.name: Storm
snapshots.subtitle: The village schoolmaster
snapshots.body: Gertrude's father and the village schoolmaster, first shown alarmed at news that a mission house may be built in the parish — worried, half-joking, about what will become of him and the church if it is.

snapshots.name: Hellgum
snapshots.subtitle: The American preacher
snapshots.body: Properly John Hellgum, a Swede who emigrated to Chicago, married a local farmer's daughter there, and returned as the leader of a small band of believers with a faith of their own — the outside figure whose arrival sets the community's religious upheaval in motion.
